topics.topic: How duplicate JsonPayload.port values are represented or reconciled in JSON objects
questions: Which passage must change, or how are duplicate JsonPayload.port values reconciled? The model permits multiple tuple entries with the same port, but a JSON object cannot contain one distinct member per such entry under the required port-based member names.

judgement.why: This asks the same duplicate-port reconciliation question on unchanged text as P1.

precedent.topic: Whether KeyFieldsContent must require unique ports or define canonical handling for duplicate-port fields
quotes: content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the idempotency_key variant MUST build one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port and holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes, so the order of the fields does not change the key, and return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; a field whose value is null is kept as null, not dropped.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
KeyFieldsContent fields (exact, no others exist): subject_kind: Literal['idempotency_key'], fields: tuple[JsonPayload, ...]
JsonPayload fields (exact, no others exist): payload_kind: Literal['json'], port: str, canonical_json: bytes
precedent.why: The texts require a member for every entry but neither prohibit duplicate ports nor define how multiple entries with the same object-member name are reconciled.

topics.topic: Whether JSON-text fields are treated as ordinary strings or parsed and canonicalized
questions: Must JSON-text fields such as value_schema remain ordinary JSON strings, in which case their contents are not passed to canonical_bytes and invalid embedded JSON cannot raise NonCanonicalValueError, or must their contents be parsed and canonicalized so that such an error can propagate?

judgement.why: This asks the same JSON-text-field treatment question on unchanged text as P13.

precedent.topic: Whether JSON-text fields must be parsed and validated or remain opaque strings
quotes: content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For every content variant of IdentitySubject (contract_version, implementation, trial_case, flow_version, stored_value, corpus) MUST build one JSON object whose members are exactly the variant's fields keyed by field name, subject_kind included, with nested models as objects keyed by field name, tuples as arrays, enum members as their value text, None as null and JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings, take its canonical bytes with canonical_bytes and return the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those bytes.
precedent.why: The passage explicitly requires JSON-text fields such as value_schema to remain JSON strings rather than being parsed as nested JSON values.

topics.topic: Whether cleanup failure overrides an earlier execute_function outcome
questions: When cleanup cannot be confirmed after a wall deadline, resource hit, or trap hit, must the earlier outcome selected by the stated precedence be returned, or must it be replaced with crashed and cleanup_failed?

When the wall deadline or a resource/process/trap condition holds and cleanup also cannot be confirmed, must the earlier outcome win under the stated first-match ordering, or must cleanup_failed override it with crashed?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about cleanup failure overriding an earlier timeout, resource-exhaustion, or sandbox-violation outcome.

precedent.topic: Whether cleanup failure overrides an earlier timeout, resource-exhaustion, or sandbox-violation outcome
quotes: An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped and the exchange directory is removed; when either cannot be confirmed the outputs are discarded and the result is outcome crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed of = models.DetailCode;
precedent.why: The mandatory cleanup result explicitly replaces the execution result with crashed and cleanup_failed whenever cleanup cannot be confirmed.

topics.topic: How multipart file parts handle a None media_type
questions: Must file-carriage input ports be required to have a non-None media_type, or must multipart file parts omit or otherwise define Content-Type when media_type is None?

judgement.why: This asks the same question about the same unchanged passages as P4.

precedent.topic: How prepare_request handles multipart file inputs with a None media_type
quotes: prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] For POST, PUT and PATCH without a file input the inputs not used in the path form one JSON object keyed by port name, sent as its RFC 8785 canonical bytes with content type application/json; with a file input the body is multipart/form-data with one part per input not used in the path in port name order, one part per file in list order for a many file port, each part having exactly the two headers Content-Disposition form-data with name set to the port, plus filename set to the port for a file part, and Content-Type, the port's media type for a file part and application/json without parameters for a value part whose content is the canonical JSON bytes.

prepare_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] An input is not placeable, giving input_not_placeable with the port named, when a placeholder value is not a non-null string or integer, or a GET or DELETE query value is not a string, integer, number, boolean, null or list of those; inputs are examined in port name order and a list's elements in list order, and the first that cannot be placed is named; an input placed in the path is placed nowhere else.

Port fields (exact, no others exist): name: str, direction: PortDirection, value_schema: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, cardinality: Cardinality, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass | None
precedent.why: The model permits a missing media type, while multipart file parts require that value and the specified placement failures do not say how this case ends.

topics.topic: Whether multipart boundary variation changes request_digest
questions: Must multipart-boundary differences also change request_digest as required by “any other difference,” or is the boundary an additional difference that must be excluded from that claim?

quotes: prepare_request: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The description lists the method, the full URL with its query, and every header sent on the wire with names lower-cased in code point order, each with its value except the credential header and content-length, which appear with value None, and a multipart content type without its boundary parameter; its body is the JSON body as text, or for multipart the parts in order each with name, filename when present, media type and the SHA-256 of the part content, so the boundary never enters it.

prepare_request: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] request_digest is content_identity of the canonical JSON of the description, so equal requests give equal digests, a rotated credential value changes nothing and any other difference changes the digest; the credential value never appears in the description, the digest or any reason.
judgement.why: One passage excludes the multipart boundary from the digest's description while the other says every difference except credential rotation changes the digest.

topics.topic: Whether an existing equal contract version above a lowered release ceiling is refused or returned unchanged
questions: When an equal stored contract version has a bound above the current release ceiling, must the call raise RefusedError or return the existing version unchanged?
Must an existing equal contract version whose bound now exceeds a lowered release ceiling be refused as the first passage requires, or returned unchanged as the second passage requires?

quotes: an existing equal contract version is returned unchanged even when a later release lowered a ceiling below its bounds (A01 rule 4, A20 rule 4).
judgement.why: The explicit exception requires returning the equal stored version unchanged despite a subsequently lowered ceiling.

topics.topic: Whether a newly admitted verdict for the already-current implementation should trigger activation
questions: When a new admitted verdict is produced for an implementation that is already the current activation, must activate be false to avoid another activation, or must it always be true for every new verdict?

judgement.why: P18 already answers the same question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Whether current implementations suppress activation and writes for new and reused admitted verdicts
quotes: An admitted verdict activates the implementation by the kernel in the same request unless it already is the contract version's current activation: a new verdict sets activate true in its change, a reused admitted verdict writes one RecordActivationChange through record_change;
precedent.why: The exception applies to an admitted verdict generally, so both new and reused admitted verdicts suppress activation and its associated write when the implementation is already current.

topics.topic: Whether cleanup failure changes a non-crashed sandbox outcome to crashed
questions: If cleanup_failed accompanies a sandbox outcome other than crashed, must the recorded outcome retain the sandbox outcome of the same name or be changed to crashed?

judgement.why: P51 already answers the same question on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Whether cleanup failure overrides every sandbox outcome and discards outputs
quotes: When the sandbox reports detail cleanup_failed the execution is recorded crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed first, and then StopRequiredError is raised so that nothing further runs in the request.

For passed and output_mismatch the outputs are recorded, a value as a StoredValue stored with put_value_bytes and a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef whose disclosure_class is the highest class of the case's inputs, every output taking that class; other outcomes record outputs None;
precedent.why: The unconditional cleanup_failed rule overrides the reported outcome with crashed, and crashed is an other outcome whose outputs are None.

topics.topic: Required handling and outcome status when a non-read SendResult has no attempt_status
questions: When a non-read SendResult has attempt_status None, must the function raise StoreInternalError without an outcome change, or must it still build and write exactly one outcome change; if the latter, what valid AttemptStatus should that change contain?

quotes: a non-read binding given authority None, or a non-read SendResult whose attempt_status is None, is a broken invariant raised as StoreInternalError, nothing sent or written for the former.
judgement.why: The text explicitly requires StoreInternalError when a non-read SendResult has no attempt_status; the no-write qualification applies only to the former case of missing authority.

topics.topic: Whether resend authorization filters approvals by attempt number relative to the latest not_applied attempt
questions: Must resend authorization exclude approved matching approvals whose attempt_number is not greater than the latest not_applied attempt, or must it select the oldest approved matching approval without that attempt-number restriction?

quotes: then only an approval whose attempt_number is greater than that of the element's latest such attempt (the highest attempt_number among them) counts, approvals requested before it never counting, no grant counts and no flow activation counts, whatever the effect class.

otherwise MUST return ApprovalAuthority for the oldest in store order of the element's approvals, read with ApprovalsOfElement, whose status is approved and whose request_digest equals the given request_digest;
judgement.divergence: One implementation excludes approvals whose attempt_number is not greater than the latest not_applied attempt; another selects the oldest approved digest-matching approval regardless of attempt_number, which changes whether the element sends or waits and is noticed by the service, owner, and caller.
judgement.why: The resend rule imposes an attempt-number condition while the authority-selection rule specifies approval eligibility using only approved status and matching request_digest.

topics.topic: Whether an over-ceiling mapped value list is delivered
questions: Must an over-ceiling mapped value list be treated as delivered, or must it never be delivered?

quotes: every delivered list of a mapped node MUST be measured before any of them is delivered or written, and when one exceeds the ceiling none of them is delivered, to a node or a flow output;
judgement.why: The text explicitly requires that an over-ceiling mapped list not be delivered.

topics.topic: Whether an undelivered empty mapped value output is stored
questions: For an empty mapped node whose value output is never delivered, must its empty-list StoredValue be written for the NodeExecution output, or must it remain unwritten until delivery?

quotes: a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's value_schema as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change;
A mapped node over an empty list executes and sends nothing and writes one NodeExecution succeeded without map_index, executed naming its pinned implementation or binding, every output an empty list;
judgement.why: One passage defers writing the StoredValue until first delivery, while the other requires an undelivered empty mapped node's NodeExecution to contain every output as an empty list.

topics.topic: Whether rejected requests must remain unread with a null response id or be parsed to recover a valid id
questions: For a body rejected by the first size check, must the body remain unread and the response id be null, or must it be parsed to preserve its string or integer id?
Must the body be read to recover the response id even when the size or token check fails, or must those refusals use null because the body cannot yet be read?
For an oversized body or failed token check, must the body remain unread, or must it be inspected to preserve a valid string or integer id in the refusal response?

judgement.why: This asks the same question about pre-body size or token failures and response IDs on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Whether pre-body failures may read the request ID or must return null
quotes: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
precedent.why: The body is not read before size and token checks, so refusals at those checks cannot recover its id and use null.

topics.topic: Whether exception messages containing sensitive diagnostic information must be preserved verbatim or sanitized
questions: When a non-internal exception's own message contains a token, service credential, host path or stack trace, must that message be preserved except for truncation, or sanitized to satisfy the disclosure prohibition?
When the unchanged reason of a startup exception contains a token, credential value, configuration content or stack trace, must serve_kernel write that reason verbatim or redact it?

quotes: Text an agent supplies — purposes, implementation code, names — is data: it is never evaluated, imported, compiled, formatted or interpreted in the kernel process; a JSON text it supplies is data too, parsed only as JSON by canonical_bytes and by the schema check of the module that judges it, never evaluated or executed; no answer and no refusal carries a token, a service credential, a host path or a stack trace, an internal error included (A16 rules 5 and 7).

The reason of every code but internal_error is the exception's own message cut to at most the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary; internal_error carries an empty reason, never the exception text, type, path or stack trace (A16 rule 7).

Every step is required: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller, the same exception with its own reason; before it propagates MUST write the failing step's name — load_installation, check_installed_instances, open_store, probe_sandbox, recover_in_flight_attempts or recover_running_runs — as one line to standard error, so the step is named there and the reason stays the exception's own; no later step runs and nothing is retried or skipped.

When run_start_sequence raises, which has already written the failing step's name, MUST write the exception's reason to standard error, without any token, credential value, configuration content or stack trace, open no entrance and return a non-zero exit code; there is no partial start and no retry.
judgement.why: The texts require preserving non-internal and startup exception reasons while also forbidding sensitive information those unchanged reasons may contain.
